notice: Immutable calibration history of DISH222. C4 is the current reference (decision D1). Every product keeps the epoch it was produced with; historical products are never relabelled. A product re-expressed on a newer epoch is a NEW dataset with a 'rederivation' record.

fractional_excess_definition.value: f = P_line / P_baseline - 1, equivalently f = 10^(x/10) - 1 for a line height of x dB above the fitted baseline

epochs.title: Relative scale: line height in dB above a fitted baseline

valid_period.note: Relative dB was the operational scale until LAB-anchored conversion factors were introduced. The start is unknown. The end marks the last supplied dataset whose products are purely in dB.

method.value: Per-spectrum baseline fit on line-free channels (V65 pipeline: bandpass self-flattening, line-free re-zeroing, beam stacking); value = peak or channel height above baseline in dB

implementation.value: Legacy V65/V67 stitcher inside the acquisition app
External processing that produced the 26 Aug CSV/XLSX/FITS files (code not supplied)
implementation.note: Neither legacy application contains a FITS, CSV or XLSX writer.

limitations.value: No temperature scale; values are internally consistent but relative
About 10-20% session-to-session scale wobble
Values depend on the persisted bandpass template and baseline choices, which were not supplied

superseded_reason.value: A LAB-anchored conversion to kelvin was introduced to compare with the LAB survey

epochs.title: LAB-anchored effective system temperature (single-point anchor through the origin)

valid_period.note: Bounded by the first products citing the LAB-anchored factor (26 Aug FITS, dated 29 Aug; validation document of 28 Aug) and the 2 Sep Y-factor calibration (C2). Exact dates are not documented.

epochs.brightness_equation: T = T_sys_eff * (10^(x/10) - 1), x = line height in dB above baseline

method.value: Anchor a measured dB value on the galactic plane to the LAB brightness at the same (l, b) convolved to a 3 deg beam; T_sys_eff = T_B(LAB) / (10^(dB/10) - 1). The factor bundles system temperature and beam efficiency.

implementation.value: V62 'LAB scale calibration' in the acquisition app, writing a stored LAB-scale calibration file (not supplied)
implementation.note: This is the only LAB-anchored method in the supplied code. That it produced the quoted 330-480 K range is inferred; the validation document also mentions an 'all-sky fit' whose code is not supplied.

limitations.value: Anchored on a single bright position and forced through the origin, so an additive pedestal cannot be detected
Varies with elevation and between sessions (330-480 K)
Depends on the external LAB profile service

superseded_reason.value: An independent Y-factor (wall to zenith) system-temperature measurement was introduced on 2 Sep 2026

epochs.title: Y-factor system temperature 179.5 K with main-beam efficiency 0.30 (2 Sep 2026)

established.note: Timestamp as written by the software, without a time zone (local time, most likely Asia/Riyadh; the zone is inferred).

valid_period.note: Used for the 1-3 Sep products; private project records indicate it was still in use for sessions on 8 and 13 Sep. Replaced by the 20 Sep hot-load measurement (C3).

epochs.brightness_equation: T_A = f * T_sys ; T_B = T_A / eta = f * G with G = T_sys / eta ; pedestal assumed zero

sources.locator: FITS header ETA_MB 'main-beam eff vs Bonn LAB'

conversion_constant_g_k.note: Computed as T_sys / eta = 179.5 / 0.30. Not stated as a single number in the sources.

pedestal_p.note: No pedestal term exists in the C2 equations.

t_hot_k.note: 50.0 degC converted with +273.15, as the V70 code does.

method.value: Wall (hot load, entered as 50 degC) versus zenith (cold sky) power ratio from the display-averaged raw spectrum; T_sys = (T_hot - T_cold) / (Y - 1). eta taken from the ratio of a 1 Sep plane map to the LAB survey.

supporting_checks.value: Recomputing T_sys from p_wall/p_zenith in the Y-factor record with the V70 formula gives 179.6 K (179.5 K recorded)
supporting_checks.note: Arithmetic check by the Phase 0 audit; confirms which formula produced the stored value.

implementation.value: V70 Kelvin calibration button (wall to zenith); V72 eta field; V71 default T_sys 179.5 K
The supplied Y-factor record was written before V72 (no eta_mb key)
implementation.note: The supplied V75 writes an eta_mb key; the supplied record has none.

limitations.value: eta = 0.30 is characteristic of a compact source under-filling the beam and inconsistent with the measured aperture efficiency of 0.58
No pedestal term; faint-sky temperatures are biased high
The Y-factor formula omits Y on the cold term; the calibration report's form gives about 8 K lower T_sys for the same Y
eta was derived from the same 1 Sep map it was then applied to, and the 2 Sep T_sys was applied to the 1 Sep scan
limitations.note: The figure is titled '1 Sep scan' with 'T_sys = 179.5 K, Y = 4.40 dB wall calibration'.

limitations.value: Galactic-centre products on this scale read about 1.6 times LAB and do not fall off the plane as expected

sources.locator: products figure, panel 'Check 2: vs Bonn LAB' (median ratio 1.62)

limitations.value: Band power used for Y was the mean over the whole band of the display-averaged spectrum; hardware gain state and sample-format linearity are unverified
limitations.note: Phase 0 audit findings S1 and S7.

superseded_reason.value: A new hot-load measurement on 20 Sep 2026 gave T_sys = 895 K; the scale in use became 895.4/0.30

unresolved.question: Why is Y = 4.40 dB on 2 Sep but 1.29 dB on 20 Sep for a comparable 50 degC wall? Hardware change, estimator change or geometry? The calibration report does not discuss the 179.5 K result.

epochs.title: 20 Sep hot-load Tsys determination with legacy eta=0.30 conversion

valid_period.note: The report describes G = 895.4/0.30 as the scale 'prior to this work' and adopts C4 on 23 Sep.

epochs.brightness_equation: T_B = f * G with G = T_sys / eta ; pedestal assumed zero

aperture_efficiency.note: Measured in the same session; later used to show that eta = 0.30 was inappropriate.

method.value: Concrete wall at 50 degC covering all reflector panels versus zenith sky; T_sys = (T_wall - Y * T_sky) / (Y - 1)

supporting_checks.value: A repeat hot-load attempt on 23 Sep gave Y = 0.12 dB (T_sys 10831 K) and was rejected because the load covered about 10% of the beam

implementation.note: The software build used on 20 Sep 2026 is not identified or supplied; it lies between V75 and V162.

limitations.value: eta = 0.30 inflated every temperature by about 1.9x; the plane read about 237 K against about 110 K in LAB
No pedestal term; a latitude +38 deg field read 80 K against 9 K in LAB
No stored products on this scale were supplied

superseded_reason.value: A sky-referenced two-parameter fit against LAB at eight positions established G and an additive pedestal

epochs.title: Sky-referenced calibration against LAB with additive pedestal (23 Sep 2026) - CURRENT REFERENCE

valid_period.note: Valid for the hardware state of 20-23 Sep 2026. The report recommends repeating the calibration monthly and after any hardware change.

tsys_k.note: Retained from the 20 Sep hot-load measurement.

eta.note: Implied by G and T_sys; consistent with the independent aperture efficiency of 0.582.

method.value: Measured fractional line depth f (median of 15 consecutive samples per position) at eight positions spanning 8-78 K of LAB brightness convolved to a 3 deg beam; least-squares fit of f against T_LAB: slope = 1/G, intercept = p

fit_data.position_note: Table 1 gives only '(b +21)'; longitude not stated

supporting_checks.value: Ordinary least squares of f = p + T_LAB/G on Table 1 reproduces G = 1454.3 K, p = 0.01742, r = 0.968 and rms 8.5 K (n - 2 degrees of freedom)
supporting_checks.note: Independent arithmetic reproduction by the Phase 0 audit. The inverse regression (T_LAB on f) would give G of about 1362 K; fit direction is a methodological choice.

supporting_checks.value: Archival fit over 392 spectra of the 22 Sep galactic-centre survey against an HI4PI-derived surrogate: G = 1016 +/- 182 K, p = 0.0224 +/- 0.0068
supporting_checks.note: The report treats the absolute scale of this check as less reliable (surrogate, not the LAB cube) and its pedestal as consistent.

supporting_checks.value: Four determinations of the pedestal range from 0.0174 to 0.0225 (mean 0.0200, s.d. 0.0029)

implementation.value: Builds V162-V166 (LAB pointing cross-correlation, live calibration verdict, whole-run fit, calibration removal with backups, hot-load raster plateau test)

limitations.value: Residual scatter of 8.5 K per measurement, set by the receiver; fields fainter than about 40 K cannot be used for verification
Linearity cannot be established (subset fits give 667 K for faint and 908 K for bright points, not significantly different)
The pedestal is applied as a constant although the baseline defect is sloped across 1419-1423 MHz, so weak lines can still be distorted
Based on eight positions from one evening; the whole-run fit is recommended as the routine calibration
Valid only for the 20-23 Sep hardware state; HackRF sample-format linearity is independently unverified
Must not be applied silently to products taken before 23 Sep; any such use creates a new, labelled re-derivation
